terms.definition: An ecosystem managed to produce food or other farm products.
terms.examiner: Farmers control abiotic and biotic factors to raise productivity.

terms.definition: The factor in shortest supply, which restricts the rate of growth.
terms.examiner: Raising any other factor has no effect until the limiting one is supplied.

terms.definition: Choosing parents with desired characteristics and breeding from them over many generations.
terms.examiner: Slow, and narrows the gene pool.

terms.definition: Transferring a gene from one species into another to give it a new characteristic.
terms.examiner: Be able to give advantages and concerns, such as gene transfer to wild relatives.

terms.definition: The mass of feed needed to produce a unit mass of livestock.
terms.examiner: Lower is more efficient; poultry and fish are lower than cattle.

terms.definition: Using a combination of cultural, biological and chemical methods, with pesticides only when pest numbers pass a threshold.
terms.examiner: Reduces pesticide use and the risk of resistance.

terms.definition: Growing a single crop over a large area.
terms.examiner: Efficient to manage but vulnerable to pests and disease and low in biodiversity.
